title: Resolve the effective device before caching capability decisions
applies_when: A capability or kernel-dispatch helper defaults to the current accelerator, especially when inputs may be on another device or the current device can change.
lesson: A no-argument cache stores the first current-device answer, not a device-independent fact. Resolve the actual device index before the per-device cache and route tensor-dependent dispatch from the tensor's device. Test both switch orders with differing capabilities, explicit-device calls, cache reuse and the non-CUDA fallback. A mocked device-query test can establish cache/key semantics without reserving GPUs; keep native operator qualification separate.
avoid_when: One homogeneous single-device process can hide this failure. A stable CUDA ordinal is a process-local identity, not a portable hardware profile or live resource allocation. Simulated capability queries do not prove mixed-hardware kernel execution, PDL compatibility or a performance gain.

evidence.note: The original supports_pdl has a no-argument lru_cache and queries the current CUDA device, exposing the stale-answer mechanism after a device switch.

Proposed, unmerged fix includes seven CPU regressions using the real standalone utility module with mocked backend/device queries. Tests cover both switch orders, explicit device indices, property-cache reuse and non-CUDA fallback. They are not native mixed-GPU or operator performance evidence.
